I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation this year. In Quzhou County, that is still the most stable way for me to earn, use my machinery efficiently, and avoid taking on too much market risk. At 63, I care more about reliability and labor control than chasing a high but uncertain return, so I will not spread myself across too many crops. My education gives me confidence to use improved seed, soil testing logic, and tighter fertilizer control instead of farming by habit alone. I will sow winter wheat first and manage it for steady grain yield with moderate water and nutrient input, then I will follow immediately with summer maize on the same land because that fits the local climate and makes full use of the season. I will use ploughing before wheat to deal with residue and improve the seedbed, then rotary tillage before maize so I can turn the field quickly after wheat harvest. I will keep fertilizer balanced instead of pushing only nitrogen, irrigate only at the key stages, and keep pesticide use limited to necessary control rather than routine spraying.
